# Stack Research: Cloud Run Deployment Reliability

**Domain:** GCP Cloud Run deployment reliability for FastAPI + LangGraph medical app
**Researched:** 2026-02-27
**Confidence:** HIGH (core stack verified via official docs and PyPI)

## Problem Statement

The existing MedGemma app works locally via Docker Compose but breaks on Cloud Run due to three interconnected failures:

1. **MLflow Cloud Run service returns 403/503** -- service-to-service auth uses raw metadata server requests with manual token caching; token expiry is not properly handled and MLflow does not receive valid ID tokens
2. **API becomes unresponsive** -- MLflow trace export 503s block threads; no timeouts on MLflow HTTP calls
3. **Protocol processing dead-letters** -- `_preflight_check()` treats MLflow as a hard dependency; if MLflow health check fails, the entire pipeline is blocked

All three stem from treating MLflow as a required dependency instead of an optional observability layer, combined with inadequate service-to-service auth handling.

## Recommended Stack

### Service-to-Service Auth

| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `google-auth` | >=2.48.0 | ID token acquisition for Cloud Run service-to-service calls | Official Google library; `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` wraps metadata server calls with proper error handling. Already a transitive dependency via `google-cloud-aiplatform`. Use this instead of raw `requests.get()` to the metadata server. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified via [official docs](https://googleapis.dev/python/google-auth/latest/user-guide.html) and [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/google-auth/)) |
| `google-auth[requests]` | (same) | `AuthorizedSession` for automatic token refresh on HTTP calls | Provides `google.auth.transport.requests.AuthorizedSession` which handles token refresh transparently. Not needed for the MLflow env-var pattern, but useful if you later add httpx-based service calls. **Confidence: HIGH** |

**IAM requirement:** The API service's Cloud Run service account needs `roles/run.invoker` on the MLflow Cloud Run service. This is the single most common cause of 403 errors. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified via [GCP official docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service)).

**Current code problem:** `_cloud_run_auth.py` uses `requests.get()` to the metadata server with manual token caching and a hardcoded 1-hour expiry. Replace with `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token(auth_req, audience)` which handles caching, retry, and error cases internally.

### Environment-Aware Configuration

| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `pydantic-settings` | >=2.13.1 | Type-safe, environment-aware configuration | Validates all env vars at startup with clear error messages. Supports `env_file`, env var prefixes, and optional GCP Secret Manager integration via `pydantic-settings[gcp-secret-manager]`. Replaces scattered `os.getenv()` calls with a single validated Settings object. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pydantic-settings/) -- v2.13.1, 2026-02-19) |

**Pattern:** Create an `AppSettings` class that declares MLflow, database, and GCS config as typed fields with sensible defaults. MLflow fields default to `None`/disabled so the app starts cleanly without MLflow.

```python
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings
from pydantic import Field

class AppSettings(BaseSettings):
    environment: str = "development"

    # Required
    database_url: str
    gcp_project_id: str
    gcp_region: str = "europe-west4"

    # Optional observability -- None means disabled
    mlflow_tracking_uri: str | None = None
    mlflow_enabled: bool = Field(default=True, description="Kill switch for MLflow")

    # Feature flags for graceful degradation
    mlflow_required_for_pipeline: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="If True, pipeline fails when MLflow is unreachable. "
                    "If False (default), pipeline continues without tracing."
    )

    model_config = {"env_file": ".env", "env_file_encoding": "utf-8"}
```

### Resilience & Graceful Degradation

| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `pybreaker` | >=1.4.1 | Circuit breakers for external service calls | Already in use in the codebase for Gemini, GCS, Vertex AI. Add an `mlflow_breaker` with the same pattern. Does NOT support native asyncio (only Tornado), but this is acceptable because MLflow calls in this codebase are synchronous (thread executor via outbox processor). **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pybreaker/) -- v1.4.1, 2025-09-21) |
| `tenacity` | >=9.1.4 | Retry with exponential backoff for transient failures | Already a dependency (>=8.2.0). Upgrade to 9.1.4 for Python 3.12+ improvements. Supports async via `AsyncRetrying`. Use for MLflow health checks and token refresh retries. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tenacity/) -- v9.1.4, 2026-02-07) |
| `httpx` | >=0.28.1 | Async HTTP client with configurable timeouts | Already a dependency. Use for MLflow health checks instead of `urllib.request.urlopen()` which has no connection pooling. Configure explicit timeouts: `httpx.Timeout(connect=3.0, read=5.0, write=5.0, pool=3.0)`. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/httpx/) -- v0.28.1) |

**Critical pattern -- MLflow as optional dependency:**

```python
# In _preflight_check(): MLflow check should WARN, not RAISE
def _preflight_check(settings: AppSettings) -> None:
    # DB and OMOP: still required, raise on failure
    _check_database()
    _check_omop()

    # MLflow: optional unless explicitly required
    if settings.mlflow_tracking_uri:
        try:
            _check_mlflow(settings.mlflow_tracking_uri)
        except DependencyCheckError:
            if settings.mlflow_required_for_pipeline:
                raise
            logger.warning("MLflow unreachable; pipeline will run without tracing")
```

### MLflow Client (Keep Existing, Add Guards)

| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `mlflow` | >=3.8.1 (dev dependency) | Full MLflow for local dev with UI | Keep as dev-only dependency for local development. The MLflow server on Cloud Run uses the official `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v2.19.0` image. **Confidence: HIGH** |

**Token refresh pattern for Cloud Run:** MLflow reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` on every API call (verified via [mlflow/mlflow#8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823) -- resolved, env var is re-read per request). The fix is simple: refresh `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` before any MLflow operation using `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()`.

```python
def _refresh_mlflow_token(audience: str) -> bool:
    """Refresh MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN using google-auth. Returns True if refreshed."""
    if not os.getenv("K_SERVICE"):  # Not on Cloud Run
        return False
    try:
        import google.auth.transport.requests
        import google.oauth2.id_token

        auth_req = google.auth.transport.requests.Request()
        token = google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token(auth_req, audience)
        os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"] = token
        return True
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to refresh MLflow ID token", exc_info=True)
        return False
```

**Alternative considered: `mlflow.tracking.request_header.abstract_request_header_provider.RequestHeaderProvider`** -- MLflow's plugin entrypoint system allows custom header providers. This is cleaner architecturally but requires packaging a plugin and registering it via `setup.py` entrypoints. The env-var approach is simpler and sufficient for this use case.

### Structured Logging (New Addition)

| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `structlog` | >=25.5.0 | Structured JSON logging for Cloud Run | Cloud Run's logging infrastructure parses JSON logs natively and routes them to Cloud Logging with severity levels. Current `logging.basicConfig()` produces unstructured text that Cloud Logging cannot parse for severity/fields. `structlog` outputs JSON in production, human-readable in development. Has a `structlog-gcp` companion for Google Cloud-specific formatting. **Confidence: MEDIUM** (verified version via [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/structlog/) -- v25.5.0; GCP integration via [structlog-gcp](https://github.com/multani/structlog-gcp) is less widely verified) |

**This is recommended but not critical.** The existing `logging` module works. Structured logging improves observability on Cloud Run but is not required to fix the deployment failures.

### Health Checks (Cloud Run Probes)

No new libraries needed. Cloud Run supports HTTP startup and liveness probes natively. The existing `/health` and `/ready` endpoints are correct. The fix is configuration:

```yaml
# In gcloud run deploy or service.yaml:
startup-probe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  timeoutSeconds: 3
  failureThreshold: 10
  periodSeconds: 5

liveness-probe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
  timeoutSeconds: 3
  failureThreshold: 3
  periodSeconds: 30
```

**Confidence: HIGH** (verified via [GCP official docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/healthchecks)).

## Supporting Libraries (Already Present, No Changes Needed)

| Library | Version | Purpose | Notes |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|
| `fastapi` | >=0.128.0 | API framework | No changes needed |
| `sqlmodel` | >=0.0.31 | ORM/database | No changes needed |
| `langgraph` | >=1.0.6 | Pipeline orchestration | No changes needed |
| `google-cloud-aiplatform` | >=1.130.0 | Vertex AI | No changes needed |
| `google-genai` | >=1.55.0 | Gemini API | No changes needed |

## Installation

```bash
# Add to pyproject.toml [project] dependencies:
uv add pydantic-settings

# Already present (verify versions):
# google-auth is a transitive dep of google-cloud-aiplatform (already installed)
# pybreaker>=1.2.0 (upgrade to >=1.4.1)
# tenacity>=8.2.0 (upgrade to >=9.1.4)
# httpx>=0.28.1 (already present)

# Optional (structured logging):
uv add structlog
# uv add structlog-gcp  # Only if you want GCP-specific log format
```

## Alternatives Considered

| Category | Recommended | Alternative | Why Not |
|----------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Service-to-service auth | `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` | Raw metadata server HTTP request (current approach in `_cloud_run_auth.py`) | Raw approach requires manual caching, expiry tracking, and error handling -- all of which are buggy in the current code. `google-auth` handles all of this. |
| Service-to-service auth | `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` | `google.auth.compute_engine.IDTokenCredentials` | `IDTokenCredentials` is lower-level and requires passing a `Request` transport object. `fetch_id_token()` auto-detects the environment and works both locally (ADC) and on Cloud Run (metadata server). |
| MLflow token refresh | Env var refresh (`os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]`) | MLflow `RequestHeaderProvider` plugin | Plugin approach requires packaging/entrypoint registration. Env var approach is simpler, verified to work per MLflow issue #8823, and the existing codebase already uses this pattern. |
| Circuit breaker | `pybreaker` (sync) | `aiobreaker` (async) | `aiobreaker` last released 2021, effectively abandoned. The MLflow calls in this codebase are synchronous (run in thread executor), so pybreaker's sync-only nature is not a limitation. |
| Circuit breaker | `pybreaker` | `purgatory` | Less adoption, smaller community. pybreaker is already in use and working for Gemini/GCS/Vertex AI breakers. |
| Configuration | `pydantic-settings` | Scattered `os.getenv()` (current approach) | Current approach has no validation, no type checking, and defaults are scattered across multiple files. `pydantic-settings` provides a single source of truth with startup validation. |
| Configuration | `pydantic-settings` | `python-decouple` | Less maintained, no Pydantic integration, no native Secret Manager support. |
| Lightweight MLflow | Keep full `mlflow` (dev) | `mlflow-tracing` (production) | `mlflow-tracing` (v3.10.0) is 95% smaller than full `mlflow` and designed for production. However, the current codebase uses `mlflow.set_experiment()`, `MlflowClient()`, and other APIs not available in `mlflow-tracing`. Migration is possible but a separate effort. **Flag for future milestone.** |
| Logging | `structlog` | `python-json-logger` | `structlog` has better async support (ContextVars), more active maintenance, and a dedicated GCP formatter. |

## What NOT to Use

| Avoid | Why | Use Instead |
|-------|-----|-------------|
| Raw `requests.get()` to metadata server for tokens | Manual caching, no retry, no error handling. The current `_cloud_run_auth.py` has a race condition in `_token_lock` and cannot recover from metadata server transient failures. | `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` |
| `urllib.request.urlopen()` for health checks | No connection pooling, no configurable timeouts per connect/read/write, blocks the thread. Used in current `_preflight_check()`. | `httpx.Client` with explicit `Timeout` |
| `aiobreaker` | Last release 2021, effectively abandoned. | `pybreaker` (already in use, sync is fine for this codebase's threading model) |
| `mlflow` as a production dependency | Full `mlflow` package is ~1GB with UI, model serving, SQL dependencies. The API service only needs tracking client. | Keep as dev dependency; production image already excludes it via `--no-dev`. If tracing overhead becomes an issue, migrate to `mlflow-tracing`. |
| Hardcoded environment checks (`os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT") == "production"`) | Scattered across files, no validation, easy to miss. | `pydantic-settings` with a single `AppSettings.environment` field |
| `--allow-unauthenticated` on MLflow Cloud Run service | The current MLflow deployment is public (or at least was deployed without IAM restrictions before). Any external caller can hit it. | Deploy MLflow with `--no-allow-unauthenticated` and grant `roles/run.invoker` to the API service's SA only. |

## Stack Patterns by Variant

**If MLflow is deployed on Cloud Run (current architecture):**
- Use `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` for token acquisition
- Refresh `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` before each batch of MLflow operations
- Add `mlflow_breaker` circuit breaker to prevent cascade failures
- Make MLflow optional in `_preflight_check()`

**If MLflow is replaced with Cloud Logging / Cloud Trace (future):**
- Remove MLflow dependency entirely
- Use `opentelemetry-sdk` + `opentelemetry-exporter-gcp-trace` for tracing
- Use `structlog` + Cloud Logging for structured logs
- This eliminates the entire service-to-service auth problem for observability

**If the API needs to call other internal Cloud Run services (future):**
- Use `google.auth.transport.requests.AuthorizedSession` for automatic token management
- Or use `httpx` with a custom auth handler that calls `fetch_id_token()`

## Version Compatibility

| Package | Compatible With | Notes |
|---------|-----------------|-------|
| `google-auth>=2.48.0` | `google-cloud-aiplatform>=1.130.0` | google-auth is a transitive dependency; no version conflict. Verify with `uv pip show google-auth`. |
| `pydantic-settings>=2.13.1` | `pydantic>=2.0` (required by FastAPI) | pydantic-settings v2 requires pydantic v2. FastAPI 0.128+ already uses pydantic v2. No conflict. |
| `tenacity>=9.1.4` | Python >=3.10 | Requires Python 3.10+; project uses 3.12. No conflict. |
| `pybreaker>=1.4.1` | Python 3.x | No known compatibility issues with any project dependencies. |
| `structlog>=25.5.0` | Python >=3.8 | No known compatibility issues. |
| `mlflow>=3.8.1` | Python >=3.10 | Dev dependency only. The MLflow Cloud Run server uses v2.19.0 Docker image -- this is the server version, not the client. Client v3.8.1 is backward-compatible with server v2.19.0 for tracking API. |

## Sources

- [GCP Cloud Run service-to-service auth](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service) -- IAM roles, Python code example (HIGH confidence)
- [google-auth User Guide](https://googleapis.dev/python/google-auth/latest/user-guide.html) -- ID token credentials, version 2.47.0 docs (HIGH confidence)
- [google-auth PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/google-auth/) -- Version 2.48.0, released 2026-01-26 (HIGH confidence)
- [GCP Get an ID token](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/get-id-token) -- `fetch_id_token()` usage (HIGH confidence)
- [MLflow issue #8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823) -- MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN is re-read per request, resolved (HIGH confidence)
- [MLflow issue #4251](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/4251) -- Token expiry handling discussion (MEDIUM confidence)
- [pydantic-settings PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pydantic-settings/) -- Version 2.13.1, released 2026-02-19 (HIGH confidence)
- [pydantic-settings docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/) -- GCP Secret Manager integration (HIGH confidence)
- [FastAPI Settings docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/settings/) -- Recommended pydantic-settings usage (HIGH confidence)
- [pybreaker PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pybreaker/) -- Version 1.4.1, Tornado-only async (HIGH confidence)
- [tenacity PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tenacity/) -- Version 9.1.4, asyncio support (HIGH confidence)
- [httpx PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/httpx/) -- Version 0.28.1 (HIGH confidence)
- [structlog PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/structlog/) -- Version 25.5.0 (HIGH confidence)
- [Cloud Run health checks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/healthchecks) -- Startup/liveness probe config (HIGH confidence)
- [MLflow Plugins docs](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/plugins/) -- RequestHeaderProvider entrypoint (MEDIUM confidence)
- [MLflow Production Tracing SDK](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/genai/tracing/lightweight-sdk/) -- mlflow-tracing package (MEDIUM confidence)
- [GCP Graceful Degradation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/reliability/graceful-degradation) -- Design patterns (HIGH confidence)

# Feature Research: Cloud Run Deployment Reliability

**Domain:** Multi-service Cloud Run deployment (API + Frontend + MLflow + Processing Pipeline)
**Researched:** 2026-02-27
**Confidence:** HIGH (verified against official GCP docs and codebase analysis)

## Feature Landscape

### Table Stakes (Must Have -- Deployment is Unreliable Without These)

| Feature | Why Expected | Complexity | Notes |
|---------|--------------|------------|-------|
| **Service-to-service IAM auth with token refresh** | MLflow Cloud Run service returns 403 because `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` is set once at startup and expires after ~1 hour. Pipeline runs that start after token expiry fail. The API's `_cloud_run_auth.py` already fetches tokens from the metadata server but only refreshes on explicit call -- no periodic or per-request refresh. | MEDIUM | MLflow reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` from env on every request (confirmed via [mlflow#8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823)). Fix: refresh `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` before each MLflow operation, or use MLflow's `RequestAuthProvider` plugin entry point to fetch a fresh ID token per request. |
| **MLflow as optional dependency (not blocking)** | Preflight check in `trigger.py` raises `DependencyCheckError` if MLflow health check fails, which dead-letters the protocol event. MLflow is observability -- it should not block clinical data processing. | LOW | Remove MLflow from `_preflight_check()`. Make MLflow tracing best-effort throughout: wrap all MLflow calls in try/except, log warnings, continue processing. The existing `MLflowRequestMiddleware` already does this pattern correctly. |
| **Startup probes for Cloud Run services** | Without startup probes, Cloud Run uses a 240-second default. The API service initializes DB, MLflow, and outbox processor at startup -- if any dependency is slow (e.g., cold-starting MLflow), the container may be killed before it is ready. | LOW | Add `--startup-probe httpGet.path=/health,httpGet.port=8080` to `gcloud run deploy`. The `/health` endpoint already exists and checks DB connectivity. |
| **Health check that distinguishes required vs optional deps** | Current `/health` returns 503 if DB is down (correct) but does not distinguish MLflow/OMOP failures. Current `/ready` requires both DB *and* OMOP, which is correct but MLflow is checked nowhere. The real issue: if MLflow is down, the API appears healthy but protocol processing silently fails. | LOW | `/health` should check only hard dependencies (DB). `/ready` should check DB + OMOP. Add a separate `/status` endpoint that reports all dependency states (DB, OMOP, MLflow, GCS, circuit breakers) for operational visibility. Already partially implemented via `_check_breakers()`. |
| **Idempotent deploy scripts** | `deploy_api.sh` uses `--set-env-vars` which replaces all env vars on every deploy. If a variable is accidentally omitted, it disappears. The script exits on first error (`set -e`) but does not validate post-deploy state. | MEDIUM | Use `gcloud run services replace` with a YAML service manifest for declarative, fully-specified deployments. This makes the deploy truly idempotent: the YAML is the source of truth. Pin secret versions (e.g., `db-url:latest` is risky; use `db-url:3`). Add post-deploy verification: check the service URL returns 200 from `/health`. |
| **Environment-aware configuration** | Deploy script sources `.env` and constructs `--set-env-vars` inline. Mixing local `.env` values with production values is error-prone (e.g., `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` vs `GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD` split). No separate staging environment config exists. | MEDIUM | Use a per-environment YAML manifest (e.g., `deploy/production.yaml`, `deploy/staging.yaml`). Secrets come from Secret Manager (already done for DB/JWT/session). Non-secret config goes in the YAML. Remove `.env` sourcing from deploy scripts entirely. |
| **Graceful shutdown of background tasks** | The outbox processor runs as a background `asyncio.Task`. On Cloud Run, SIGTERM gives 10 seconds before SIGKILL. The lifespan handler awaits `processor.stop()` then waits for `_running_tasks`, but if the pipeline is mid-execution (Gemini API calls), 10 seconds may not be enough. | MEDIUM | Set `--timeout` (request timeout) and `--termination-grace-period` appropriately in Cloud Run config. The outbox processor should checkpoint in-progress work and mark events for retry rather than losing progress. LangGraph checkpointing (already used via `thread_id`) helps here. |

### Differentiators (Nice-to-Have for Production Quality)

| Feature | Value Proposition | Complexity | Notes |
|---------|-------------------|------------|-------|
| **MLflow `RequestAuthProvider` plugin** | Instead of manually refreshing `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` env var, implement a proper MLflow client auth plugin that fetches a fresh Cloud Run ID token from the metadata server on each request. Eliminates token expiry entirely. | MEDIUM | Register via `mlflow.request_auth_provider` entry point. Set `MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH` env var to activate. More robust than env var manipulation but requires packaging as a plugin. |
| **Minimum instances (min=1) for API service** | Eliminates cold start for user-facing API. Users currently wait 5-30s on first request after idle period. | LOW | `gcloud run deploy --min-instances=1`. Costs ~$5-15/month for a small instance. Worth it for the primary API service. MLflow and processing can stay at 0. |
| **Startup CPU boost** | Reduces cold start time for N->N+1 scaling by temporarily increasing CPU allocation during startup. | LOW | `gcloud run deploy --cpu-boost`. Free for the first 10 seconds of startup. Combine with min-instances for best UX. |
| **Traffic splitting for safe deploys** | Deploy new revision with `--no-traffic`, verify via revision URL, then shift traffic. Enables instant rollback. | LOW | Use `gcloud run deploy --no-traffic` then `gcloud run services update-traffic`. Low effort, high safety. |
| **YAML service manifests** | Replace imperative `gcloud run deploy --set-env-vars ...` with declarative YAML. Version-controlled, diffable, reviewable. Uses `gcloud run services replace service.yaml`. | MEDIUM | One YAML per service per environment. Follows Knative serving API format. This is the standard production pattern for Cloud Run. |
| **Circuit breaker for MLflow client** | The existing `resilience.py` has breakers for Gemini, GCS, UMLS, Vertex AI -- but not MLflow. If MLflow is down, every trace export attempt blocks for timeout duration. | LOW | Add `mlflow_breaker` to `resilience.py`. Wrap MLflow trace operations. When open, skip tracing silently. Already have the pattern from other breakers. |
| **Deploy verification step** | After `gcloud run deploy`, automatically hit `/health` to verify the new revision is serving correctly. If not, roll back to previous revision. | LOW | Add `curl -f $SERVICE_URL/health` after deploy. On failure: `gcloud run services update-traffic SERVICE --to-revisions=PREVIOUS=100`. |
| **Structured logging with Cloud Logging integration** | Cloud Run automatically captures stdout/stderr, but structured JSON logs integrate with Cloud Logging filters and alerting. | LOW | Use `python-json-logger` or `google-cloud-logging`. Set `LOG_FORMAT=json` in production. Already using `logging.basicConfig()` -- switch to JSON formatter when `ENVIRONMENT=production`. |
| **Liveness probes** | Detect and restart containers that become unresponsive (e.g., stuck MLflow connection, exhausted connection pool). | LOW | `--liveness-probe httpGet.path=/health,httpGet.port=8080,periodSeconds=30`. Restarts the container if `/health` fails 3 times. |
| **Dedicated service accounts per service** | Currently using default Compute Engine SA for all services. Violates least-privilege. | MEDIUM | Create `api-sa@`, `mlflow-sa@`, `frontend-sa@`. Grant only needed roles: API gets Cloud SQL Client + GCS + Vertex AI + run.invoker (for MLflow). MLflow gets Cloud SQL Client + GCS. Frontend gets nothing extra. |

### Anti-Features (Commonly Requested, Often Problematic)

| Feature | Why Requested | Why Problematic | Alternative |
|---------|---------------|-----------------|-------------|
| **MLflow behind IAP (Identity-Aware Proxy)** | Seems like the "proper" way to secure MLflow UI access | IAP adds complexity to service-to-service auth (requires OIDC audience, not the service URL). Breaks `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` auth flow. Overkill for internal-only MLflow. | Keep MLflow as `--no-allow-unauthenticated` (IAM-only). Service-to-service via ID tokens. Human access via `gcloud run services proxy mlflow`. |
| **Cloud Run service mesh / Envoy sidecar** | "Proper" service mesh with automatic mTLS and service discovery | Massive complexity overhead for 3-4 services. Cloud Run mesh is designed for large microservice deployments. Direct HTTP calls with ID tokens are simpler and sufficient. | Direct service-to-service calls with ID tokens from metadata server. |
| **Multi-region deployment** | High availability across regions | This is a hackathon/clinical trial tool, not a global SaaS product. Multi-region doubles cost and adds data residency complexity (clinical data). Single region with Cloud Run's built-in redundancy is sufficient. | Single region (europe-west4). Cloud Run provides zone-level redundancy within the region. |
| **Custom domain with managed SSL** | Professional look with custom domain | Adds DNS management, certificate provisioning complexity. Cloud Run provides `*.run.app` domains with automatic TLS. | Use the default `*.run.app` domains. Add custom domain only when needed for production user-facing URLs. |
| **Terraform / Pulumi for infrastructure** | Infrastructure as code is "best practice" | For 3-4 services, Terraform adds a dependency (state management, provider versions, plan/apply workflow) without proportional benefit. YAML manifests + deploy scripts are simpler and sufficient. | YAML service manifests versioned in git + shell deploy scripts. Graduate to Terraform only if infrastructure grows beyond 10+ resources. |
| **Pub/Sub for inter-service communication** | Event-driven architecture pattern | The outbox processor pattern already handles async event processing within the API service. Adding Pub/Sub means managing subscriptions, dead-letter topics, and ordering guarantees for minimal benefit when services are co-located in the same region. | Keep the outbox pattern for intra-service async processing. Consider Pub/Sub only if services need to be independently deployable units (not current architecture). |
| **MLflow required in preflight checks** | "Ensure observability is always working" | MLflow is observability, not business logic. Requiring it means a tracing server outage blocks clinical data processing. This is the current bug causing dead-lettered protocol events. | Make MLflow best-effort. Log warnings when unavailable. Never block pipeline execution on MLflow availability. |
| **Automatic MLflow scaling** | "MLflow should handle production load" | MLflow tracking server is designed for metadata and light artifact storage, not high-throughput workloads. Auto-scaling MLflow wastes money. | Set MLflow `--max-instances=1` (or 2). It handles metadata writes sequentially. If trace volume becomes an issue, batch writes or use async export. |

## Feature Dependencies

```
[Service-to-Service IAM Auth]
    |
    +--requires--> [Dedicated Service Accounts] (differentiator, but auth works with default SA)
    |
    +--enables---> [MLflow RequestAuthProvider Plugin]
    |
    +--enables---> [MLflow as Optional Dependency]

[MLflow as Optional Dependency]
    |
    +--requires--> [Circuit Breaker for MLflow] (to avoid timeout-blocking on failed traces)
    |
    +--enhances--> [Health Check Separation] (to surface MLflow state without blocking)

[Idempotent Deploy Scripts]
    |
    +--enables---> [YAML Service Manifests] (manifests make scripts trivially idempotent)
    |
    +--enables---> [Traffic Splitting for Safe Deploys]
    |
    +--enables---> [Deploy Verification Step]

[Environment-Aware Configuration]
    |
    +--requires--> [Idempotent Deploy Scripts] (config must be declarative before it can be env-aware)

[Startup Probes]
    |
    +--enhances--> [Health Check Separation] (probes use health endpoints)
    |
    +--complements-> [Liveness Probes]

[Minimum Instances] --conflicts-- [Cost Optimization]
    (min=1 costs money but eliminates cold starts; choose per service)
```

### Dependency Notes

- **Service-to-Service Auth requires nothing else first:** The existing `_cloud_run_auth.py` already fetches tokens. The fix is making refresh automatic/periodic, not adding new infrastructure.
- **MLflow as Optional requires Circuit Breaker:** Without a breaker, each failed MLflow call blocks for the timeout duration. The breaker ensures fast-fail after threshold.
- **YAML Manifests enable everything else in the deploy pipeline:** Once manifests exist, traffic splitting, verification, and environment-aware config are straightforward additions.
- **Minimum Instances conflicts with Cost Optimization:** Set min=1 for API (user-facing), min=0 for MLflow and processing (background services).

## MVP Definition

### Launch With (v1) -- Fix What's Broken

- [x] **MLflow as optional dependency** -- Remove from preflight checks, wrap all MLflow calls in try/except. This is the #1 fix: protocol processing should never dead-letter because tracing is down.
- [x] **Service-to-service auth token refresh** -- Refresh `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` before each pipeline run (not just at startup). Use the existing `configure_mlflow_auth()` which already refreshes from metadata server.
- [x] **Health check separation** -- `/health` = DB only (required). `/ready` = DB + OMOP (required for full functionality). MLflow state in response body but not blocking.
- [x] **Startup probes** -- Add `--startup-probe` to deploy commands for API and MLflow services.

### Add After Validation (v1.x) -- Harden the Deployment

- **MLflow version mismatch**: Cloud Run Dockerfile uses v2.19.0, docker-compose uses v3.9.0. The production deployment lacks async logging available in v3.x.
- **Security gap**: MLflow Cloud Run is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated` while the `_cloud_run_auth.py` module already implements ID token acquisition for authenticated calls.

### Roadmap Implications

**Phase 1 (Decouple MLflow)** should be first -- it resolves all three stated problems with minimal code changes and no infrastructure work. It involves: adding `mlflow_breaker` to `resilience.py`, removing MLflow from `_preflight_check()`, moving `_cleanup_orphan_traces()` out of module scope, and wrapping `pipeline_span()`/`llm_span()` with circuit breaker fallback.

**Phase 2 (Service Auth)** and **Phase 3 (Health Probes)** can be done in parallel after Phase 1.

**Phase 4 (Version Alignment)** depends on Phase 1 being in place -- async logging helps but does not replace circuit breaking.

### Open Questions

- What is the actual production MLflow version? The Dockerfile says v2.19.0 but docker-compose says v3.9.0. This determines whether async logging env vars are available.
- Should MLflow be behind IAM authentication? The `_cloud_run_auth.py` module exists but MLflow is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated`. This is a security decision that affects the auth hardening phase.
- What is the acceptable trace data loss rate? If MLflow is down for an hour, all traces from that period are lost. Is this acceptable, or should traces be buffered to disk for later replay?

input.content:
# Pitfalls Research

**Domain:** GCP Cloud Run deployment -- FastAPI + MLflow tracing + service-to-service auth + async background processing
**Researched:** 2026-02-27
**Confidence:** HIGH (based on codebase analysis + official GCP docs + MLflow docs + project's own resolved/unresolved issues)

## Critical Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: MLflow Synchronous Trace Export Blocks the Entire API

**What goes wrong:**
Every incoming HTTP request passes through `MLflowRequestMiddleware`, which calls `mlflow.start_span()`. When the MLflow tracking server is unreachable (503), the synchronous trace export blocks the request handler, consuming the single-threaded uvicorn worker. After a few concurrent requests, all workers are stuck waiting on MLflow network timeouts, and the API becomes completely unresponsive -- even `/health` stops responding.

**Why it happens:**
MLflow's default trace logging is synchronous. The middleware (`middleware.py`) wraps every request in `mlflow.start_span()`, which attempts to flush span data to the tracking server on span close. When the server returns 503 or times out, the flush blocks for the full network timeout (default ~30s). This is invisible locally because Docker Compose MLflow is always available and responds instantly.

**How to avoid:**
1. Set `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true` as an environment variable on the Cloud Run API service. This makes trace export non-blocking (available since MLflow 2.16.0; the project uses v2.19.0).
2. Configure `MLFLOW_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING_MAX_WORKERS=5` and `MLFLOW_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING_RETRY_TIMEOUT=10` (not the default 500s) to limit resource consumption.
3. Add a circuit breaker around `mlflow.start_span()` in the middleware so that after 3 consecutive failures, tracing is disabled for 60 seconds (consistent with the project's existing `pybreaker` pattern in `shared/resilience.py`).
4. The middleware already has a fallback (`if not app_called: await self.app(scope, receive, send)`), but it only catches exceptions, not slow network calls. The async logging setting is the real fix.

**Warning signs:**
- API `/health` endpoint starts timing out after deployment even though the database is healthy.
- Cloud Run logs show repeated `MLflow request tracing failed` warnings.
- Cloud Run metrics show increasing request latency (50th percentile jumps from <100ms to 30s+).
- Container restarts increase (Cloud Run kills unresponsive instances).

**Phase to address:**
Phase 1 (immediate) -- This is the root cause of the "API unresponsive" issue. A single env var (`MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true`) plus a reduced retry timeout resolves it.

---

### Pitfall 2: MLflow Preflight Check Makes Protocol Processing a Hard Dependency on Observability

**What goes wrong:**
`_preflight_check()` in `trigger.py` (lines 296-361) checks MLflow health before every pipeline run. When MLflow is unreachable, it raises `DependencyCheckError`, which causes the outbox event to fail and eventually dead-letter after 3 retries. Every protocol upload immediately fails -- not because extraction is broken, but because the tracing server is down.

**Why it happens:**
The preflight check was designed to prevent wasted Gemini API calls when infrastructure is down. The mistake was treating MLflow (an observability tool) as a hard infrastructure dependency alongside the database and OMOP vocabulary (which ARE required for the pipeline to produce results). The check conflates "can we trace this pipeline run" with "can we run this pipeline at all."

**How to avoid:**
1. Make the MLflow health check in `_preflight_check()` a soft check: log a warning if unreachable but do NOT raise `DependencyCheckError`. Keep the DB and OMOP checks as hard failures.
2. In `_ensure_mlflow()`, return `False` gracefully (already does) but also set a module-level flag that `pipeline_span()` can check to skip tracing entirely for this run.
3. The two hard checks (PostgreSQL, OMOP) remain -- those are genuinely required for the pipeline to persist results.

**Warning signs:**
- All protocol uploads immediately go to `extraction_failed` or `dead_letter` status.
- Error reason contains "MLflow tracking server" or "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI."
- Pipeline never reaches the `ingest` node (no Gemini API calls logged).
- This ONLY happens in Cloud Run, never locally (Docker Compose MLflow is always up).

**Phase to address:**
Phase 1 (immediate) -- Remove MLflow from the hard preflight check. This directly unblocks protocol processing.

---

### Pitfall 3: Cloud Run Service-to-Service Auth Token Expires After 1 Hour Without Refresh

**What goes wrong:**
`_cloud_run_auth.py` fetches an ID token from the GCP metadata server and sets `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` as an environment variable. The token has a 1-hour lifetime. The token is cached in `_cached_token` with `_token_expiry = now + 3600`, and `configure_mlflow_auth()` refreshes it if called again. However, `configure_mlflow_auth()` is only called at two points: (a) API startup in `lifespan()` and (b) inside `_preflight_check()` before each pipeline run. The MLflow middleware (`MLflowRequestMiddleware`) does NOT refresh the token. After 1 hour, every request's trace export sends an expired token, gets 403, and the middleware falls into the error path.

**Why it happens:**
MLflow reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` from the environment on every request. The token is a Cloud Run ID token (JWT) with a 1-hour expiry. The `_cloud_run_auth` module has refresh logic, but it is not called from the hot path (request middleware). The MLflow Python client has an open feature request ([FR #8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823)) for refreshable tokens -- it does not exist yet.

**How to avoid:**
1. Add a periodic token refresh: start a background thread or async task in `lifespan()` that calls `configure_mlflow_auth()` every 45 minutes (before the 1-hour expiry, accounting for the 5-minute margin already in `_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN`).
2. Alternatively, if MLflow is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated` (as shown in DEPLOYMENT.md section 4.6a), no token is needed at all. Evaluate whether the MLflow service needs IAM protection -- if it is only accessed by the API service within the same project, `--allow-unauthenticated` with VPC or IAP may be simpler.
3. If keeping IAM auth, also call `configure_mlflow_auth()` from the middleware error handler when a 403 is detected, so it self-heals.

**Warning signs:**
- MLflow works fine for the first ~55 minutes after deployment, then starts returning 403.
- Cloud Run logs show "Could not fetch ID token" or "MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN" errors.
- The API becomes unresponsive ~1 hour after deployment (combines with Pitfall 1).

**Phase to address:**
Phase 1 or Phase 2 -- If MLflow is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated`, this pitfall disappears entirely. If IAM auth is required, add the periodic refresh in Phase 2.

---

### Pitfall 4: `--set-secrets` Wipes All Existing Secrets on Cloud Run Update

**What goes wrong:**
Running `gcloud run services update api --set-secrets "NEW_SECRET=name:latest"` replaces the ENTIRE secret map with only the listed secret. This silently removes `DATABASE_URL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, and `OMOP_VOCAB_URL`. The next revision crashes at startup with "DATABASE_URL environment variable is required but not set."

**Why it happens:**
`--set-secrets` is a destructive replacement operation (like Kubernetes `kubectl set`), not an additive one. Developers expect `--set-secrets "X=..."` to add X to the existing secrets, but it replaces the whole map. The safe alternative `--update-secrets` adds/updates without removing others. This exact issue already bit this project (documented in DEPLOYMENT.md section 4.4).

**How to avoid:**
1. Always use `--update-secrets` and `--update-env-vars` for incremental changes.
2. Only use `--set-secrets` / `--set-env-vars` in the deploy script where ALL values are explicitly listed (the deploy_api.sh already does this correctly with `^||^` delimiter).
3. Add a comment in the deploy script: `# WARNING: --set-secrets replaces ALL secrets. Always list every secret the service needs.`
4. Consider adding a pre-deploy check in the script that verifies the secret list includes the required keys.

**Warning signs:**
- API crashes immediately after a `gcloud run services update` command.
- Error: "DATABASE_URL environment variable is required but not set."
- The revision shows only the newly added secret in Cloud Console.

**Phase to address:**
Phase 1 (already documented in DEPLOYMENT.md, but the deploy script should enforce this -- add validation).

---

### Pitfall 5: Cloud Run `--set-env-vars` Comma Delimiter Breaks Values Containing Commas

**What goes wrong:**
Environment variable values containing commas (like CORS origins: `https://app1.run.app,https://app2.run.app`) get split into separate env var assignments. The second origin becomes a malformed env var like `https://app2.run.app=""`, and CORS fails silently for the second origin.

**Why it happens:**
`gcloud run deploy --set-env-vars` uses comma (`,`) as the default delimiter between key=value pairs. When a value itself contains a comma, gcloud parses it as a separator. This is a documented GCP behavior but extremely easy to hit.

**How to avoid:**
1. Use the `^DELIM^` syntax to override the delimiter. The deploy script already uses `^||^` as the delimiter (line 92 of `deploy_api.sh`). This is correct.
2. Never use bare `--set-env-vars "KEY1=val1,KEY2=val2"` when any value might contain commas.
3. For manual `gcloud run services update` commands, document the delimiter requirement prominently.

**Warning signs:**
- CORS errors for specific origins but not others.
- Env var inspection shows truncated values or extra spurious env vars.
- Frontend can reach the API from one origin but not another.

**Phase to address:**
Already resolved in the deploy script. Phase 1 validation: ensure all manual update instructions also use the `^||^` pattern.

---

### Pitfall 6: Cloud Run Outbox Processor Background Task Gets Throttled Without Always-On CPU

**What goes wrong:**
Cloud Run's default billing mode is "request-based" -- CPU is only allocated while processing HTTP requests. The `OutboxProcessor` runs as an `asyncio.Task` in the background, polling the database every 1 second. Between HTTP requests, Cloud Run throttles CPU to near-zero, so the outbox processor stops polling. Protocols appear stuck in `pending` status indefinitely. They process only when an unrelated HTTP request comes in and wakes the CPU.

**Why it happens:**
Cloud Run's request-based billing model allocates CPU only during active request processing. The outbox pattern (poll DB -> process events in background) is a background processing pattern that requires CPU between requests. This is a fundamental mismatch between the serverless request-response model and the long-polling background worker pattern.

**How to avoid:**
1. Deploy the API service with `--no-cpu-throttling` (instance-based billing / always-on CPU). This keeps CPU allocated even between requests, enabling the outbox processor to poll continuously.
2. Alternatively, if cost is a concern, move the outbox processor to a separate Cloud Run service or Cloud Run job that runs on a schedule (Cloud Scheduler triggers it every minute). This isolates the background processing cost.
3. Set `--min-instances=1` alongside `--no-cpu-throttling` to prevent cold starts from also delaying protocol processing.

**Warning signs:**
- Protocols stay in `pending` status for long periods, then suddenly process in bursts when new HTTP requests arrive.
- Cloud Run metrics show near-zero CPU utilization between request spikes, but the outbox poll interval is 1 second.
- Processing latency is highly variable and correlates with traffic patterns rather than queue depth.

**Phase to address:**
Phase 2 -- After MLflow issues are resolved, this becomes the next reliability concern. Add `--no-cpu-throttling` to the deploy script.

## Technical Debt Patterns

Shortcuts that seem reasonable but create long-term problems.

| Shortcut | Immediate Benefit | Long-term Cost | When Acceptable |
|----------|-------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Deploying MLflow with `--allow-unauthenticated` | No service-to-service auth complexity | MLflow UI/API publicly accessible on the internet; anyone can read experiment data or write traces | Only if the MLflow service has no sensitive data (protocol names, patient identifiers in traces), or if behind IAP/VPC. Acceptable for hackathon demo; unacceptable for production with real clinical data. |
| Using default Compute Engine service account for all services | One SA, no IAM complexity | Over-privileged: every Cloud Run service gets every role (Secret Manager, Vertex AI, Cloud SQL, GCS). Breach of one service compromises all. | Acceptable for development/hackathon. Replace with per-service SAs before any real clinical data flows. |
| `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` via `os.environ` mutation | Simple, works immediately | Global env mutation is not thread-safe in theory (CPython's GIL protects in practice). Multiple threads reading/writing env vars simultaneously could race. | Acceptable for now since `configure_mlflow_auth()` uses a thread lock on the cached token. Monitor if you add more workers. |
| In-process outbox processor (no separate worker) | Single deployment unit, simple architecture | Couples request serving with background processing; request latency spikes when pipeline is CPU-intensive; OOM risk when multiple protocols process simultaneously | Acceptable during hackathon. Move to dedicated worker (Cloud Run Jobs or separate service) for production. |

## Integration Gotchas

Common mistakes when connecting to external services.

| Integration | Common Mistake | Correct Approach |
|-------------|----------------|------------------|
| MLflow on Cloud Run | Assuming MLflow accepts access tokens (OAuth2 tokens from `gcloud auth print-access-token`). MLflow on Cloud Run needs an **ID token** with the service URL as the audience. | Use `gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=MLFLOW_URL` or fetch from metadata server with `?audience=MLFLOW_URL`. The `_cloud_run_auth.py` module does this correctly. |
| MLflow on Cloud Run | Deploying MLflow without `--allow-unauthenticated` but forgetting to grant `roles/run.invoker` to the API service account on the MLflow service. | Either deploy with `--allow-unauthenticated` OR explicitly grant: `gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding mlflow --member="serviceAccount:$API_SA" --role=roles/run.invoker`. |
| Cloud SQL from Cloud Run | Using `localhost:5432` in the database URL (works locally, fails on Cloud Run). | Use Unix socket: `postgresql://user:pass@/dbname?host=/cloudsql/CONNECTION_NAME`. The project handles this correctly in Secret Manager. |
| GCS signed URLs | Generating signed URLs without `iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob` permission on the service account. Works locally with user credentials (which have owner role), fails on Cloud Run. | Grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to the service account. Already resolved in this project. |
| MLflow experiment "0" deleted | MLflow's default experiment (ID "0") can be soft-deleted. If traces land before `set_experiment()` runs, they target experiment "0" and get 400 errors. | The codebase already handles this by restoring experiment "0" if deleted (in `_init_mlflow()` and `_ensure_mlflow()`). |
| Cloud Run env var `ENVIRONMENT=production` | Forgetting to set this, so the API uses `dev-session-secret` as the session secret. The code raises `RuntimeError` at startup if `ENVIRONMENT=production` and the default secret is used. | Always include `ENVIRONMENT=production` in the deploy command. Already in the deploy script. |

## Performance Traps

Patterns that work at small scale but fail as usage grows.

| Trap | Symptoms | Prevention | When It Breaks |
|------|----------|------------|----------------|
| Synchronous MLflow tracing on every HTTP request | Increasing P99 latency; API timeouts; eventual unresponsiveness | Set `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true`; add circuit breaker around trace calls | Immediately -- even 1 slow MLflow response blocks a request for 30s |
| `OutboxProcessor` with `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` | Two concurrent pipelines consuming all CPU/memory; other protocols queue indefinitely; OOM on heavy protocols | Limit to 1 worker for 1Gi memory containers; implement backpressure; monitor memory | At 3+ simultaneous protocol uploads on a 1Gi instance |
| MLflow `_cleanup_orphan_traces()` at module import time | Module import of `trigger.py` blocks for network call to MLflow; delays startup and outbox processor initialization | Move orphan cleanup to a background task or make it lazy (run on first pipeline invocation, not import) | When MLflow is slow/cold-starting (30s+), every import of trigger.py blocks |
| Cloud Run cold starts with database migrations | `alembic upgrade head` runs on every container start; if schema is already current, it still checks migration state, adding 2-5s to cold start | Run migrations in CI/CD or a one-off Cloud Run Job, not in the container CMD | At 10+ containers scaling simultaneously, all hitting the DB for migration locks |

## Security Mistakes

Domain-specific security issues beyond general web security.

| Mistake | Risk | Prevention |
|---------|------|------------|
| MLflow `--allow-unauthenticated` with clinical data in traces | Anyone on the internet can browse experiment data (protocol names, extraction results, potentially PHI) | Deploy MLflow behind IAM + grant only the API service account `roles/run.invoker`. Or use IAP for human access to the MLflow UI. |
| `SESSION_SECRET` as default `dev-session-secret` in production | Session cookies can be forged; any user can impersonate any other | The code already blocks this (`RuntimeError` if production + default secret). Ensure ENVIRONMENT=production is always set. |
| `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` in `os.environ` visible in `/proc/*/environ` | Token leak if container is compromised | For hackathon this is acceptable. For production, use a custom MLflow auth plugin with credential refresh, not env var injection. |
| GCS signed URLs with long expiry | Signed download URLs for protocol PDFs accessible to anyone with the URL for the expiry duration | Set short expiry (15 minutes). Verify the current `generate_signed_url` call uses a short `expiration`. |

## UX Pitfalls

Common user experience mistakes in this domain (from the API consumer / operator perspective).

| Pitfall | User Impact | Better Approach |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| Protocol upload succeeds but extraction silently dead-letters | User uploads a PDF, sees "processing", waits indefinitely, then eventually sees "dead_letter" with no actionable error | Return the error category in the protocol status response. If MLflow preflight fails, show "Processing service temporarily unavailable, please retry in a few minutes" instead of dead-lettering. |
| Health endpoint returns 200 but extraction is broken | Operator sees `/health` reporting "healthy" but protocols fail. `/health` only checks the database, not MLflow or Gemini availability. | Add MLflow reachability to `/health` as informational (not blocking 200). Or add a dedicated `/health/pipeline` endpoint that tests the full preflight. |
| Deploy wipes CORS origins | After a `--set-env-vars` update, CORS breaks because the previous CORS_ORIGINS was dropped. Users see opaque CORS errors in the browser console. | Use `--update-env-vars` for incremental changes. Include CORS_ORIGINS in every full deploy command. |

## "Looks Done But Isn't" Checklist

Things that appear complete but are missing critical pieces.

- [ ] **MLflow service deployed:** Often missing IAM invoker binding for the API service account -- verify `gcloud run services get-iam-policy mlflow --region $REGION` includes the API SA with `roles/run.invoker` (or `--allow-unauthenticated`).
- [ ] **API deploy succeeds:** Often missing `--no-cpu-throttling` for background outbox processing -- verify with `gcloud run services describe api --region $REGION --format='value(spec.template.metadata.annotations["run.googleapis.com/cpu-throttling"])'`.
- [ ] **CORS configured:** Often missing the GCS bucket CORS policy for direct browser uploads -- verify `gsutil cors get gs://BUCKET_NAME` returns the correct JSON with `origin`, `method`, and `responseHeader` entries.
- [ ] **MLflow token works at deploy time:** Often missing periodic refresh -- verify token is still valid after 1 hour by checking Cloud Run logs for 403 errors.
- [ ] **Secrets all present:** After any `gcloud run services update`, verify all 5 secrets are mounted: `gcloud run services describe api --region $REGION --format='yaml(spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)'` and confirm DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, JWT_SECRET_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, OMOP_VOCAB_URL are all present.
- [ ] **MLflow async logging configured:** After enabling `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true`, verify it takes effect: check Cloud Run logs during a request burst for absence of "MLflow request tracing failed" warnings.

## Recovery Strategies

When pitfalls occur despite prevention, how to recover.

| Pitfall | Recovery Cost | Recovery Steps |
|---------|---------------|----------------|
| API unresponsive due to MLflow blocking | LOW | 1. `gcloud run services update api --region $REGION --update-env-vars "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="` to unset MLflow. 2. Deploy new revision. 3. Re-enable after fixing MLflow. Alternative: just add `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true`. |
| All protocols dead-lettered | MEDIUM | 1. Fix MLflow or remove it from preflight. 2. Reset dead-letter events: `UPDATE outbox_events SET status='pending', retry_count=0 WHERE status='dead_letter';` 3. Reset protocol status: `UPDATE protocols SET status='pending' WHERE status='dead_letter';` |
| Secrets wiped by `--set-secrets` | LOW | 1. `gcloud run services update api --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,GOOGLE_API_KEY=google-api-key:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"` -- one command restores all. 2. Traffic routes to new revision automatically. |
| Token expired, MLflow returning 403 | LOW | 1. If using `--allow-unauthenticated`, no token needed -- check MLflow deploy config. 2. If using IAM auth, redeploy API (restart refreshes token on startup). 3. Long-term: add periodic refresh task. |
| CPU throttling starves outbox processor | LOW | `gcloud run services update api --region $REGION --no-cpu-throttling` -- single command, creates new revision. |
| Cold start takes >60s due to MLflow init | LOW | MLflow init is already deferred to a background thread. If still slow, unset `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` temporarily. |

## Pitfall-to-Phase Mapping

How roadmap phases should address these pitfalls.

| Pitfall | Prevention Phase | Verification |
|---------|------------------|--------------|
| MLflow sync trace blocking (#1) | Phase 1: Add `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true` to deploy env vars | After deploy, send 10 concurrent requests while MLflow is down. API should respond to all within 1s. |
| MLflow hard preflight (#2) | Phase 1: Remove MLflow from `_preflight_check()` hard requirements | Upload a protocol with `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` set to an unreachable URL. Protocol should process successfully (no tracing, but extraction + persist work). |
| ID token expiry (#3) | Phase 2: Add periodic token refresh OR deploy MLflow with `--allow-unauthenticated` | Leave API running for 2+ hours. Check Cloud Run logs for 403 errors from MLflow. None should appear. |
| `--set-secrets` wipe (#4) | Phase 1: Add validation to deploy script; document in deploy playbook | Run `gcloud run services describe api` after every deploy and verify all 5 secrets are present. |
| Comma delimiter in env vars (#5) | Already resolved | Verify `deploy_api.sh` uses `^||^` delimiter (it does). |
| CPU throttling on outbox (#6) | Phase 2: Add `--no-cpu-throttling` to deploy script | Upload a protocol with no concurrent HTTP traffic. It should process within 2 minutes (not wait for the next request). |

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Project:** MedGemma -- Cloud Run Deployment Reliability
**Mode:** Ecosystem (Stack dimension)
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **Service-to-service auth fix is straightforward:** Replace raw metadata server HTTP calls in `_cloud_run_auth.py` with `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` from the `google-auth` library (already a transitive dependency). The API service account needs `roles/run.invoker` on the MLflow service.
- **MLflow token refresh works via env var:** MLflow re-reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` on every API call (confirmed via resolved GitHub issue #8823). Simply update `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` before MLflow operations using `fetch_id_token()`.
- **MLflow must become optional:** The `_preflight_check()` in `trigger.py` treats MLflow as a hard dependency (`raise DependencyCheckError` if unreachable). This must change to a warning with a `mlflow_required_for_pipeline` configuration flag (default: False).
- **`pydantic-settings` centralizes config:** Replace scattered `os.getenv()` calls with a validated `AppSettings` class. Version 2.13.1 supports GCP Secret Manager natively via extras.
- **No new circuit breaker library needed:** `pybreaker` (already in use, v1.4.1) is correct for this codebase's threading model. Add an `mlflow_breaker` alongside existing Gemini/GCS/Vertex AI breakers.

### Files Created

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/.planning/research/STACK.md` | Technology recommendations for Cloud Run deployment reliability |

### Confidence Assessment

| Area | Level | Reason |
|------|-------|--------|
| Service-to-service auth | HIGH | Verified via official GCP docs and google-auth library docs |
| MLflow token refresh | HIGH | Confirmed via resolved GitHub issue with maintainer verification |
| Configuration management | HIGH | pydantic-settings is FastAPI's official recommendation, verified on PyPI |
| Circuit breakers | HIGH | pybreaker already in use, verified version on PyPI |
| Structured logging | MEDIUM | structlog version verified, but GCP integration (structlog-gcp) has less community validation |

### Roadmap Implications

1. **Phase 1: Make MLflow optional** -- Change `_preflight_check()` to warn instead of raise. Add `mlflow_breaker` circuit breaker. This alone fixes the dead-lettering problem.
2. **Phase 2: Fix service-to-service auth** -- Replace `_cloud_run_auth.py` with `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()`. Ensure IAM binding for `roles/run.invoker`.
3. **Phase 3: Centralize configuration** -- Introduce `pydantic-settings` `AppSettings` class. Add environment-aware defaults and feature flags.
4. **Phase 4: Add timeouts and structured logging** -- Replace `urllib.request.urlopen()` with `httpx.Client`, add Cloud Run startup/liveness probes, optionally add structlog.

### Open Questions

- **MLflow server version mismatch:** The MLflow Docker image is v2.19.0 but the client in dev deps is >=3.8.1. This client-server version gap works for tracking API but should be verified for trace export specifically.
- **`mlflow-tracing` migration:** The lightweight `mlflow-tracing` package (95% smaller) could replace full `mlflow` in production. This requires assessing which MLflow APIs the codebase actually uses in production vs dev-only. Flag for a future milestone.
- **Cloud Run min-instances:** If the MLflow service cold-starts take 30s+, consider setting `--min-instances=1` to avoid cold start latency. This has cost implications that need evaluation.

    54→    # Feature flags for graceful degradation
    55→    mlflow_required_for_pipeline: bool = Field(
    56→        default=False,
    57→        description="If True, pipeline fails when MLflow is unreachable. "
    58→                    "If False (default), pipeline continues without tracing."
    59→    )
    60→
    61→    model_config = {"env_file": ".env", "env_file_encoding": "utf-8"}
    62→```
    63→
    64→### Resilience & Graceful Degradation
    65→
    66→| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
    67→|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
    68→| `pybreaker` | >=1.4.1 | Circuit breakers for external service calls | Already in use in the codebase for Gemini, GCS, Vertex AI. Add an `mlflow_breaker` with the same pattern. Does NOT support native asyncio (only Tornado), but this is acceptable because MLflow calls in this codebase are synchronous (thread executor via outbox processor). **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pybreaker/) -- v1.4.1, 2025-09-21) |
    69→| `tenacity` | >=9.1.4 | Retry with exponential backoff for transient failures | Already a dependency (>=8.2.0). Upgrade to 9.1.4 for Python 3.12+ improvements. Supports async via `AsyncRetrying`. Use for MLflow health checks and token refresh retries. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tenacity/) -- v9.1.4, 2026-02-07) |
    70→| `httpx` | >=0.28.1 | Async HTTP client with configurable timeouts | Already a dependency. Use for MLflow health checks instead of `urllib.request.urlopen()` which has no connection pooling. Configure explicit timeouts: `httpx.Timeout(connect=3.0, read=5.0, write=5.0, pool=3.0)`. **Confidence: HIGH** (verified [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/httpx/) -- v0.28.1) |
    71→
    72→**Critical pattern -- MLflow as optional dependency:**
    73→
    74→```python
    75→# In _preflight_check(): MLflow check should WARN, not RAISE
    76→def _preflight_check(settings: AppSettings) -> None:
    77→    # DB and OMOP: still required, raise on failure
    78→    _check_database()
    79→    _check_omop()
    80→
    81→    # MLflow: optional unless explicitly required
    82→    if settings.mlflow_tracking_uri:
    83→        try:
    84→            _check_mlflow(settings.mlflow_tracking_uri)
    85→        except DependencyCheckError:
    86→            if settings.mlflow_required_for_pipeline:
    87→                raise
    88→            logger.warning("MLflow unreachable; pipeline will run without tracing")
    89→```
    90→
    91→### MLflow Client (Keep Existing, Add Guards)
    92→
    93→| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
    94→|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
    95→| `mlflow` | >=3.8.1 (dev dependency) | Full MLflow for local dev with UI | Keep as dev-only dependency for local development. The MLflow server on Cloud Run uses the official `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v2.19.0` image. **Confidence: HIGH** |
    96→
    97→**Token refresh pattern for Cloud Run:** MLflow reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` on every API call (verified via [mlflow/mlflow#8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823) -- resolved, env var is re-read per request). The fix is simple: refresh `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` before any MLflow operation using `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()`.
    98→
    99→```python
   100→def _refresh_mlflow_token(audience: str) -> bool:
   101→    """Refresh MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN using google-auth. Returns True if refreshed."""
   102→    if not os.getenv("K_SERVICE"):  # Not on Cloud Run
   103→        return False
   104→    try:
   105→        import google.auth.transport.requests
   106→        import google.oauth2.id_token
   107→
   108→        auth_req = google.auth.transport.requests.Request()
   109→        token = google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token(auth_req, audience)
   110→        os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"] = token
   111→        return True
   112→    except Exception:
   113→        logger.warning("Failed to refresh MLflow ID token", exc_info=True)
   114→        return False
   115→```
   116→
   117→**Alternative considered: `mlflow.tracking.request_header.abstract_request_header_provider.RequestHeaderProvider`** -- MLflow's plugin entrypoint system allows custom header providers. This is cleaner architecturally but requires packaging a plugin and registering it via `setup.py` entrypoints. The env-var approach is simpler and sufficient for this use case.
   118→
   119→### Structured Logging (New Addition)
   120→
   121→| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
   122→|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
   123→| `structlog` | >=25.5.0 | Structured JSON logging for Cloud Run | Cloud Run's logging infrastructure parses JSON logs natively and routes them to Cloud Logging with severity levels. Current `logging.basicConfig()` produces unstructured text that Cloud Logging cannot parse for severity/fields. `structlog` outputs JSON in production, human-readable in development. Has a `structlog-gcp` companion for Google Cloud-specific formatting. **Confidence: MEDIUM** (verified version via [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/structlog/) -- v25.5.0; GCP integration via [structlog-gcp](https://github.com/multani/structlog-gcp) is less widely verified) |
   124→
   125→**This is recommended but not critical.** The existing `logging` module works. Structured logging improves observability on Cloud Run but is not required to fix the deployment failures.
   126→
   127→### Health Checks (Cloud Run Probes)
   128→
   129→No new libraries needed. Cloud Run supports HTTP startup and liveness probes natively. The existing `/health` and `/ready` endpoints are correct. The fix is configuration:
   130→
   131→```yaml
   132→# In gcloud run deploy or service.yaml:
   133→startup-probe:
   134→  httpGet:
   135→    path: /health
   136→  initialDelaySeconds: 5
   137→  timeoutSeconds: 3
   138→  failureThreshold: 10
   139→  periodSeconds: 5
   140→
   141→liveness-probe:
   142→  httpGet:
   143→    path: /health
   144→  timeoutSeconds: 3
   145→  failureThreshold: 3
   146→  periodSeconds: 30
   147→```
   148→
   149→**Confidence: HIGH** (verified via [GCP official docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/healthchecks)).
   150→
   151→## Supporting Libraries (Already Present, No Changes Needed)
   152→
   153→| Library | Version | Purpose | Notes |
   154→|---------|---------|---------|-------|
   155→| `fastapi` | >=0.128.0 | API framework | No changes needed |
   156→| `sqlmodel` | >=0.0.31 | ORM/database | No changes needed |
   157→| `langgraph` | >=1.0.6 | Pipeline orchestration | No changes needed |
   158→| `google-cloud-aiplatform` | >=1.130.0 | Vertex AI | No changes needed |
   159→| `google-genai` | >=1.55.0 | Gemini API | No changes needed |
   160→
   161→## Installation
   162→
   163→```bash
   164→# Add to pyproject.toml [project] dependencies:
   165→uv add pydantic-settings
   166→
   167→# Already present (verify versions):
   168→# google-auth is a transitive dep of google-cloud-aiplatform (already installed)
   169→# pybreaker>=1.2.0 (upgrade to >=1.4.1)
   170→# tenacity>=8.2.0 (upgrade to >=9.1.4)
   171→# httpx>=0.28.1 (already present)
   172→
   173→# Optional (structured logging):
   174→uv add structlog
   175→# uv add structlog-gcp  # Only if you want GCP-specific log format
   176→```
   177→
   178→## Alternatives Considered
   179→
   180→| Category | Recommended | Alternative | Why Not |
   181→|----------|-------------|-------------|---------|
   182→| Service-to-service auth | `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` | Raw metadata server HTTP request (current approach in `_cloud_run_auth.py`) | Raw approach requires manual caching, expiry tracking, and error handling -- all of which are buggy in the current code. `google-auth` handles all of this. |
   183→| Service-to-service auth | `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` | `google.auth.compute_engine.IDTokenCredentials` | `IDTokenCredentials` is lower-level and requires passing a `Request` transport object. `fetch_id_token()` auto-detects the environment and works both locally (ADC) and on Cloud Run (metadata server). |
   184→| MLflow token refresh | Env var refresh (`os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]`) | MLflow `RequestHeaderProvider` plugin | Plugin approach requires packaging/entrypoint registration. Env var approach is simpler, verified to work per MLflow issue #8823, and the existing codebase already uses this pattern. |
   185→| Circuit breaker | `pybreaker` (sync) | `aiobreaker` (async) | `aiobreaker` last released 2021, effectively abandoned. The MLflow calls in this codebase are synchronous (run in thread executor), so pybreaker's sync-only nature is not a limitation. |
   186→| Circuit breaker | `pybreaker` | `purgatory` | Less adoption, smaller community. pybreaker is already in use and working for Gemini/GCS/Vertex AI breakers. |
   187→| Configuration | `pydantic-settings` | Scattered `os.getenv()` (current approach) | Current approach has no validation, no type checking, and defaults are scattered across multiple files. `pydantic-settings` provides a single source of truth with startup validation. |
   188→| Configuration | `pydantic-settings` | `python-decouple` | Less maintained, no Pydantic integration, no native Secret Manager support. |
   189→| Lightweight MLflow | Keep full `mlflow` (dev) | `mlflow-tracing` (production) | `mlflow-tracing` (v3.10.0) is 95% smaller than full `mlflow` and designed for production. However, the current codebase uses `mlflow.set_experiment()`, `MlflowClient()`, and other APIs not available in `mlflow-tracing`. Migration is possible but a separate effort. **Flag for future milestone.** |
   190→| Logging | `structlog` | `python-json-logger` | `structlog` has better async support (ContextVars), more active maintenance, and a dedicated GCP formatter. |
   191→
   192→## What NOT to Use
   193→
   194→| Avoid | Why | Use Instead |
   195→|-------|-----|-------------|
   196→| Raw `requests.get()` to metadata server for tokens | Manual caching, no retry, no error handling. The current `_cloud_run_auth.py` has a race condition in `_token_lock` and cannot recover from metadata server transient failures. | `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` |
   197→| `urllib.request.urlopen()` for health checks | No connection pooling, no configurable timeouts per connect/read/write, blocks the thread. Used in current `_preflight_check()`. | `httpx.Client` with explicit `Timeout` |
   198→| `aiobreaker` | Last release 2021, effectively abandoned. | `pybreaker` (already in use, sync is fine for this codebase's threading model) |
   199→| `mlflow` as a production dependency | Full `mlflow` package is ~1GB with UI, model serving, SQL dependencies. The API service only needs tracking client. | Keep as dev dependency; production image already excludes it via `--no-dev`. If tracing overhead becomes an issue, migrate to `mlflow-tracing`. |
   200→| Hardcoded environment checks (`os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT") == "production"`) | Scattered across files, no validation, easy to miss. | `pydantic-settings` with a single `AppSettings.environment` field |
   201→| `--allow-unauthenticated` on MLflow Cloud Run service | The current MLflow deployment is public (or at least was deployed without IAM restrictions before). Any external caller can hit it. | Deploy MLflow with `--no-allow-unauthenticated` and grant `roles/run.invoker` to the API service's SA only. |
   202→
   203→## Stack Patterns by Variant
   204→
   205→**If MLflow is deployed on Cloud Run (current architecture):**
   206→- Use `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` for token acquisition
   207→- Refresh `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` before each batch of MLflow operations
   208→- Add `mlflow_breaker` circuit breaker to prevent cascade failures
   209→- Make MLflow optional in `_preflight_check()`
   210→
   211→**If MLflow is replaced with Cloud Logging / Cloud Trace (future):**
   212→- Remove MLflow dependency entirely
   213→- Use `opentelemetry-sdk` + `opentelemetry-exporter-gcp-trace` for tracing
   214→- Use `structlog` + Cloud Logging for structured logs
   215→- This eliminates the entire service-to-service auth problem for observability
   216→
   217→**If the API needs to call other internal Cloud Run services (future):**
   218→- Use `google.auth.transport.requests.AuthorizedSession` for automatic token management
   219→- Or use `httpx` with a custom auth handler that calls `fetch_id_token()`
   220→
   221→## Version Compatibility
   222→
   223→| Package | Compatible With | Notes |
   224→|---------|-----------------|-------|
   225→| `google-auth>=2.48.0` | `google-cloud-aiplatform>=1.130.0` | google-auth is a transitive dependency; no version conflict. Verify with `uv pip show google-auth`. |
   226→| `pydantic-settings>=2.13.1` | `pydantic>=2.0` (required by FastAPI) | pydantic-settings v2 requires pydantic v2. FastAPI 0.128+ already uses pydantic v2. No conflict. |
   227→| `tenacity>=9.1.4` | Python >=3.10 | Requires Python 3.10+; project uses 3.12. No conflict. |
   228→| `pybreaker>=1.4.1` | Python 3.x | No known compatibility issues with any project dependencies. |
   229→| `structlog>=25.5.0` | Python >=3.8 | No known compatibility issues. |
   230→| `mlflow>=3.8.1` | Python >=3.10 | Dev dependency only. The MLflow Cloud Run server uses v2.19.0 Docker image -- this is the server version, not the client. Client v3.8.1 is backward-compatible with server v2.19.0 for tracking API. |
   231→
   232→## Sources
   233→
   234→- [GCP Cloud Run service-to-service auth](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service) -- IAM roles, Python code example (HIGH confidence)
   235→- [google-auth User Guide](https://googleapis.dev/python/google-auth/latest/user-guide.html) -- ID token credentials, version 2.47.0 docs (HIGH confidence)
   236→- [google-auth PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/google-auth/) -- Version 2.48.0, released 2026-01-26 (HIGH confidence)

   238→- [MLflow issue #8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823) -- MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN is re-read per request, resolved (HIGH confidence)
   239→- [MLflow issue #4251](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/4251) -- Token expiry handling discussion (MEDIUM confidence)
   240→- [pydantic-settings PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pydantic-settings/) -- Version 2.13.1, released 2026-02-19 (HIGH confidence)
   241→- [pydantic-settings docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/) -- GCP Secret Manager integration (HIGH confidence)
